name: Business · US single-member LLC
for: a freelancer or consultant billing through a US single-member LLC taxed as a disregarded entity (Schedule C)

accounts.description: Schedule C Part I: gross receipts less returns, plus other income
Gross receipts or sales (Schedule C line 1); check against the Forms 1099 you receive
Hourly and day-rate work
Milestone and fixed-price engagements
Recurring fees, maintenance contracts, SaaS revenue
Digital products, licences, royalties
Costs re-billed to clients at cost; the matching cost sits in Contractors and direct costs:Client-billable costs
Schedule C line 2: refunds and price reductions. Contra-revenue, so a debit balance
Refunds and credit notes issued to clients
Discounts granted after invoicing
Schedule C line 6
Interest on the business bank account
Prizes and awards related to the business, recovered bad debts, grants
Schedule C Part II, grouped by the line each cost lands on. Owner draws and contributions are equity, not expenses; federal income tax and self-employment tax are the owner's, not the LLC's
What it costs to deliver the work
Independent contractors (line 11); file Form 1099-NEC for $600 or more paid to a non-corporate contractor

accounts.path: Expenses:Contractors and direct costs:Subcontracted firms and agencies
accounts.description: Companies you subcontract parts of an engagement to (line 11 or 27a)

accounts.path: Expenses:Contractors and direct costs:Commissions and referral fees
accounts.description: Line 10
Costs incurred for a client and re-billed at cost; matched by Revenue:Reimbursed expenses billed
Tools and infrastructure (line 18 office expense or line 27a other expenses)
SaaS seats, licences, app subscriptions

accounts.path: Expenses:Software and cloud:Cloud hosting and infrastructure
accounts.description: AWS, GCP, Azure, Vercel, servers, CDN

accounts.path: Expenses:Software and cloud:Domains, email and web services
accounts.description: Domain renewals, email hosting, DNS, certificates

accounts.path: Expenses:Software and cloud:Data, APIs and AI services
accounts.description: Metered API usage, data feeds, model providers
Schedule C line 8
Search, social and sponsored placements

accounts.path: Expenses:Marketing and advertising:Website, content and design
accounts.description: Site design, copywriting, branding, portfolio

accounts.path: Expenses:Marketing and advertising:Events, sponsorships and networking
accounts.description: Meetups, sponsorships, promotional materials
Deductible up to $25 per recipient per year (Pub 463)
Schedule C line 17: fees charged by accountants and attorneys that are ordinary and necessary for the business
Contracts, trademarks, disputes

accounts.path: Expenses:Legal and professional:Tax preparation and advice
accounts.description: The business part of tax advice and return preparation; the personal part is not a business expense

accounts.path: Expenses:Legal and professional:Registered agent and compliance services
accounts.description: Registered agent and filing services; the state fees themselves go to Taxes and licenses
Banks, processors and interest
Account and wire fees (line 27a)

accounts.path: Expenses:Bank and payment fees:Payment processing fees
accounts.description: Stripe, PayPal, merchant and invoicing fees (line 10 or 27a)

accounts.path: Expenses:Bank and payment fees:FX and international transfer fees
accounts.description: Conversion and transfer fees; exchange-rate differences post to the system FX gain/loss account
Business credit card and loan interest (line 16b)
Schedule C line 23: state and local taxes on the business, licences and regulatory fees. Not here: federal income tax, self-employment tax, sales tax collected from buyers

accounts.path: Expenses:Taxes and licenses:State LLC annual fees and reports
accounts.description: Annual report and registration fees in the formation state and any foreign-qualified state

accounts.path: Expenses:Taxes and licenses:State franchise and LLC taxes
accounts.description: Flat state LLC taxes, e.g. Delaware's $300 annual tax due June 1 or California's $800 annual tax

accounts.path: Expenses:Taxes and licenses:Business licenses and permits
accounts.description: City and county business licences, professional permits

accounts.path: Expenses:Taxes and licenses:Sales and other business taxes
accounts.description: Sales tax owed as seller, personal property tax on business assets, gross receipts taxes
Schedule C line 15, insurance other than health. The owner's health insurance is a Schedule 1 deduction, not a business expense
Overnight business travel (line 24a), meals (line 24b) and the car (line 9)

accounts.path: Expenses:Travel and meals:Airfare and long-distance transport
accounts.description: Flights, trains and buses between your tax home and the business destination (line 24a)
Hotels while away overnight on business (line 24a)

accounts.path: Expenses:Travel and meals:Local transport, taxis and rideshare
accounts.description: Taxis, rideshare, transit and airport transfers on business trips (line 24a)
Meals with a business contact or while travelling on business; generally only 50% is deductible (line 24b, Pub 463). Book the full cost here and let the return apply the limit
Line 9: standard mileage rate (70 cents per mile for 2025) or the business share of actual costs
Business parking and tolls, deductible on top of the mileage rate
Where the work happens

accounts.path: Expenses:Office and workspace:Office rent and coworking
accounts.description: Rent or lease of office space and coworking memberships (line 20b)
Line 30: simplified method ($5 per square foot up to 300 sq ft) or actual expenses on Form 8829

accounts.path: Expenses:Office and workspace:Office supplies and postage
accounts.description: Line 18 (office expense) and line 22 (supplies consumed)

accounts.path: Expenses:Office and workspace:Utilities, phone and internet
accounts.description: Line 25, business share only; the base rate of the first home phone line is not deductible
Line 21: incidental repairs that do not add value or extend life
Hardware and furniture. Items up to $2,500 per invoice or item can be expensed under the de minimis safe harbor; above that they are depreciated (line 13, Form 4562, section 179)
Laptops, monitors, phones, peripherals
Desk, chair, lighting
Rent or lease of equipment and machinery (line 20a)
Cables, adapters, tools with a life under a year (line 22)
Line 27a; deductible when it maintains or improves skills in your present work, not when it qualifies you for a new trade (Topic 513)

accounts.path: Expenses:Education and professional development:Courses and training
Expenses:Education and professional development:Books and publications
accounts.description: Books, journals, paid newsletters

accounts.path: Expenses:Education and professional development:Conferences and seminars
accounts.description: Registration fees; the travel to get there goes to Travel and meals

accounts.path: Expenses:Education and professional development:Professional dues and memberships
accounts.description: Professional associations, certifications, licence renewals
Schedule C line 27a, plus non-deductible items kept visible
Invoices written off; deductible only if previously included in income (accrual method)
Government penalties and fines are not deductible; kept separate so they can be added back
Anything else ordinary and necessary that fits no other group
